# glinet_wan_access (Resource)

Manages the access to the router from the WAN (remote access): the web UI over HTTPS, SSH and ping (`firewall.set_wan_access` in the router API). The router has one WAN access configuration, so use one instance of this resource.

~> **Warning:** this resource can cut the management of the router over the WAN: when `https` or `ssh` is `false`, or when `whitelist_enabled` is `true` and the whitelist does not have your address, you cannot get access to the web UI, the API or SSH from the WAN. The access from the LAN does not change. When `https` or `ssh` is `true`, the router is open to the WAN on that service; use the whitelist to limit the sources.

Each write sends all attributes, as the web UI does. When `whitelist_enabled` or `whitelist` is not set, the provider sends back the router value that it reads just before the write. After the write, the web UI reads the firewall rules again: it is not known whether the write adds or changes firewall rules, and so changes the positional IDs of the firewall rules and port forwards on the router. `glinet_firewall_rule` and `glinet_firewall_port_forward` look up the router ID before each call, so they do not keep an ID in the state. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy disables the access from the WAN: the provider sends `false` for `https`, `ssh`, `ping` and `whitelist_enabled`, and an empty whitelist.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_wan_access" "this" {
  https             = true
  ssh               = false
  ping              = true
  whitelist_enabled = true

  # IP address = description
  whitelist = {
    "203.0.113.10" = "office"
    "2001:db8::10" = ""
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `https` (Boolean) Whether the web UI and the API of the router accept connections over HTTPS from the WAN (`enable_https` in the router API).
- `ping` (Boolean) Whether the router answers ping from the WAN (`enable_ping` in the router API).
- `ssh` (Boolean) Whether the SSH server of the router accepts connections from the WAN (`enable_ssh` in the router API). The web UI shows this switch only while SSH is enabled on the LAN (`ssh_enabled` of `glinet_local_access`). The provider does not check this.

### Optional

- `whitelist` (Map of String) Addresses that have the access from the WAN when `whitelist_enabled` is `true` (`whitelist` in the router API). Each key is an IPv4 or IPv6 address without a prefix length (`ipaddr`), and each value is a description of at most 64 characters, or `""` (`name`). It is not known whether the router accepts an address with a prefix length. The provider sends the addresses in the order of the keys. When the router has an address two times, the provider keeps only one of them in a write. When it is not set, the router value does not change. Set it to `{}` to remove all addresses.
- `whitelist_enabled` (Boolean) Whether only the addresses in `whitelist` have the access from the WAN (`enable_whitelist` in the router API). The web UI shows this switch only while `https`, `ssh` or `ping` is `true`. When it is not set, the router value does not change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `wan_access`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "wan_access".
terraform import glinet_wan_access.this wan_access
```
